Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
In article <3r9mpn$c...@nntp4.u.washington.edu>,

Semprini <ska...@u.washington.edu> wrote:
>I had Lucian robbing people all over the place. He blocked a forced-to-hunt
>minion that had a Flak Jacket. At close range, Lucian stole the flak
>jacket. Could he use it to prevent the 1 damage done by the blocked
>vampire? We said yes, but it has a really funny thing to imagine.

Not unless he stole it with First Strike. Since the strikes
resolve simutaneously, the damage will hit him before(or as) he gets
the Flak Jacket, but just before he spends a blood to heal that damage.

Messages.Author: George Fink
Messages.Body:
This brings up a question.

Suppose my opponent has a flamethrower, or other such awesome
equipment. I'm attacking, and my opponent blocks with that vampire.

I'm not afraid, because i've got a fast hands card (steal weapon with
first strike at superior). I slap it down.

My opponent only has normal celerity, but he plays another fast hands
to attempt to steal the flamethrower back; since he's only got normal
celerity its not a first strike.

The question is, who has the flamethrower at the end of the battle?

--George

Well, he can attempt to steal weapon even when Lucian has no weapon, but
must announce the target along with the strike. He cannot target his own
Flame Thrower, so must simply steal nothing. (A hand strike would be a
better choice, but...) Net effect is still: Lucian gets the FT.

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
When you play a strike like Fast Hands, you must choose a piece of equipment
that the other minion has as you play the card. You don't wait until the
strike resolves. So if only one minion has a Flamethrower when strikes are
declared, the other minion is the only one that can try to steal or break
a Flamethrower.

Messages.Author: Joseph Cochran
Messages.Body:
In article <GFINK.95J...@avalon.cs.ucdavis.edu>,
George Fink <gf...@avalon.cs.ucdavis.edu> wrote:
>Suppose my opponent has a flamethrower, or other such awesome
>equipment. I'm attacking, and my opponent blocks with that vampire.
>I'm not afraid, because i've got a fast hands card (steal weapon with
>first strike at superior). I slap it down.
>My opponent only has normal celerity, but he plays another fast hands
>to attempt to steal the flamethrower back; since he's only got normal
>celerity its not a first strike.
>
>The question is, who has the flamethrower at the end of the battle?

Here's my take: when you declare the strike, you have to
declare a legal strike. If it's steal equipment, the opponent has to

have that piece of equipment in order to use the strike. So in strike
declaration, you can say "I'll steal the flamethrower," but your
opponent can't, because you vampire doesn't have one to steal. In other
words, I don't think that he can call that strike, as there's nothing to
steal. And you get the FT.

>(See quoted text). therefore, the flamethrower would be in the stealer's
>possession (the strike would have resolved) by the time the second steal
>came around to resolution, and be a legal target. by that logic, the

But you have to declare the strike during strike declaration, at
which time there's no FT for the other guy to target. While Scott is
right and you *can* go after nothing, whatever you go after has to be on
the guy you're going after, so the FT is not available for theft.
First strike doesn't matter until strike resolution, which is
after the declaration is over, and that makes it too late for the
opponent to name FT.

Gord Culleton <bg...@FreeNet.Carleton.CA> wrote:
>Ok, I've been folowing this thread for a while, and this makes
>sense. By this ruling, a Steal/Destroy Equip./Weapon used as
>an additional strike would be legal? Eg. Tatiana steals Anvil's
>.44 with Sup. Celerity, thus depriving poor Anvil a strike. Anvil
>Blurs, punches Tatiana for being a knob, then steals the gun back.
>That has happened in a game. Was it legal?

Yep, that's perfectly fine, if Anvil's got the cards to do it.
Likewise, if Tatiana had the cards, she could call additional strikes to
fire the gun. I suppose that if it got really silly, if they both
played for two additional strikes, then Anvil could steal the gun back,
and then Tatiana could steal it back again! The blocker would have an
advantage, though, and would be able to hit (why use the gun if you know
that it'll be stolen). But it'd be fun to watch...

>Nope. You can't use a weapon for a strike unless you started the round
>of combat with it. [DTR, I believe]

Not correct. Stealing a weapon with first strike neutralizes any strike
just declared for it (unless that was at first strike to), but you could
fire that weapon later that round if you meet all the requirements.
